_comment: The World Labs Gaussian splat lane, as a graph the JEV graph guard judges. The strategic decision - which node lands FIRST - is made by JEV from the evidence, not asserted by the seat. Run: python harness/harness2/compositor.py --mode graph --input harness/harness2/worldlabs_graph.json --wave worldlabs-intake
_evidence: docs/intake/worldlabs-gaussian-pipeline-audit.md (VERIFIED-RUNTIME, 11/11 corrections hold on 22.0.400). The raw records are harness/probes/worldlabs_blueprint_records.json (68 calls, STRICT run dies at line 27) and harness/probes/worldlabs_pipeline_verification.json.
_probes_not_yet_written: Four nodes name a probe in owner_files that DOES NOT EXIST YET: harness/probes/worldlabs_wiring_probe.py (WIRE-INPUTS), worldlabs_upaxis_probe.py (WL-UP-AXIS), worldlabs_deliverable_probe.py (WL-DELIVERABLE) and worldlabs_desert_probe.py (WL-DESERT). owner_files names the file a node WILL own, so the path is the work item's target, not a record of a shipped probe. Every other file listed in this graph is in the tree. The four open questions stay open because their probes have not been written - and because WL-UP-AXIS, WL-DELIVERABLE and WL-DESERT additionally need a real World Labs export, which no probe can conjure.
_correction_2026_10_22: The first version of this graph said the repo's node catalogue is 'wrong for three Houdini 22 node types'. That was the audit's own retracted claim. The catalogue is FAITHFUL - every audited type matches the live build exactly, Jaccard 1.000. The hazard is a CONSUMER one: createNode() hands back a different type than the catalogue key names. The graph below carries the corrected premise, and CAT-TYPES is the corrected work item.
objective: A World Labs Gaussian splat pipeline proposed for SYNAPSE does not run: its script dies on the third node creation it makes, and eight of its prose claims are not implemented by its own code. The repo's node catalogue needs no correction - but three consumer rules do, and the lane's remaining open questions need a real World Labs export. Land the evidence first, then the repo-side truth, then the lane.
standards: Law 1: every check must be able to fail. A check that cannot fail is deleted rather than kept green.
Law 2: no number without a producer path. Every figure names the command or probe that produces it.
Law 3: status describes what happened, not what was intended.
Probe truth beats pinned constants: where the live build disagrees with a catalogue, the live build wins and the catalogue is fixed.
One owner per file. Two nodes that claim the same file compete; a conflict is a finding, not a race.
Absence of a symbol from a table is not proof of absence. The decisive test is calling it on an instance.
No hardcoded user paths. Install and every probe must work on a clean machine.

nodes.title: Land the World Labs audit, the transcribed blueprint and the self-verifying corrected pipeline
nodes.why: The blueprint's own script was transcribed into the tree and executed against 22.0.400. It dies at line 27 - the third node creation it makes, and the first that raises - and six of its calls raise while ten of its parameter writes name parameters that do not exist. Eight prose claims are unimplemented; six of those are measured by counting the terms each claim would need in the source. The corrected pipeline proves all eleven ledger entries on every run (--verify, 11/11). Nothing else about this lane can be judged until the evidence is in the tree, because every other node cites it.

nodes.title: Publish the node catalogue's CONSUMER RULES: alias resolution and the spare-parm convention
nodes.why: The catalogue is the repo's node-type authority and it is FAITHFUL: six audited types match the live build exactly, Jaccard 1.000, so no regeneration is warranted. The hazard is a consumer one. createNode('gltf') hands back gltf::2.0 and createNode('distantlight') hands back distantlight::2.0, so 14 of 17 and 58 of 123 parm names read from the unversioned entries do not exist on the node you actually get. Separately, 7,155 of 152,918 catalogue parm names (4.7%) carry a '#', Houdini's spare-parameter convention, and a script cannot set them. Consumers need both rules written down; the catalogue needs no change.

nodes.title: Add an instance-probe rule to the phantom lint for hou.Node members
nodes.why: Class-level dir(hou.Node) exposes 146 members and hasattr(hou.Node, 'parm') is False, while the instance call works. The same method says no about parm, setParms, cook and addParm, which all work. A phantom check built on class-level dir() produces false positives and false negatives on the same class, so absence from the symbol table is not conclusive for hou.Node members.

nodes.title: Record that a node reports ZERO inputs until one is wired, and stop reading input counts off a fresh node
nodes._probe_status: TO BE WRITTEN - harness/probes/worldlabs_wiring_probe.py is not in the tree yet
nodes.why: distantlight::2.0, karmarendersettings and usdrender_rop all report inputs() == [] while unwired, and all three accept the blueprint's connection. The first version of the audit read that zero as 'the call will fail' and filed three working connections as defects; a second draft of the corrected script dropped two more edges on the same false premise. A node's input count is not knowable from a fresh instance - read it after wiring, or read the catalogue's inputLabels.

nodes.title: Settle the up-axis conversion for a World Labs export (WL-EX-05)
nodes._probe_status: TO BE WRITTEN - harness/probes/worldlabs_upaxis_probe.py is not in the tree yet
nodes.why: The blueprint claims a UsdGeom.XformOp fix that its own code does not contain - the term scan finds no XformOp, no xform, no upaxis and no convert in its 140 lines - and the repo's intake already rejected a prior blueprint for assuming Y-up where Marble is +Y-down. No World Labs asset was available to the audit, so the correct conversion is UNKNOWN. Inventing one would be worse than leaving it open.

nodes.title: Settle what produces the .mp4 the blueprint promises
nodes._probe_status: TO BE WRITTEN - harness/probes/worldlabs_deliverable_probe.py is not in the tree yet
nodes.why: usdrender_rop has no video or ffmpeg output parm - only an image sequence - and the blueprint never writes output_mov, it prints a line saying it is exporting. The headline deliverable does not exist. Whether a real export or a different ROP is the answer is a fact provable from a probe, not a judgement.

nodes.title: Settle what consumes the desert half of the transition the blueprint promises
nodes._probe_status: TO BE WRITTEN - harness/probes/worldlabs_desert_probe.py is not in the tree yet
nodes.why: The deliverable is a desert-to-jungle TRANSITION, but only the jungle side is ever connected: the wrangle takes normals_jungle, normals_desert has no consumer, and desert_collider_glb is accepted by the blueprint's own signature and never used by its body. The desert half of the transition is never rendered. What consumes it is a fact provable from a probe, not a judgement.

nodes.title: Fold the World Labs lane into the ratified blueprint intake
nodes.why: The repo's own intent document is ratified:false and says every node name is V0 until a probe prints it. The audit has now produced that probe for the external blueprint. Folding the result in is the point of the intake - but it waits on the open questions, because writing the answer before it is known is how a false record gets made.
